title: AI Regulation, Compliance & Enterprise Controls 2025
description: Practical regulatory and compliance guidance for enterprises deploying AI systems, with emphasis on the EU AI Act, GPAI obligations, and operational governance controls.

articles.title: EU AI Act implementation is phased, not instantaneous
articles.summary: The EU AI Act introduces staged obligations, which means enterprises need a roadmap instead of a one-time compliance project.
key_points: The EU AI Act entered into force in 2024 with phased obligations through 2027
Prohibited practices apply from February 2, 2025
GPAI obligations apply from August 2, 2025
High-risk system obligations escalate from August 2, 2026
Remaining obligations and enforcement milestones continue into 2027

articles.title: General-purpose AI providers face distinct obligations
articles.summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models are expected to maintain documentation, support downstream deployers, and address copyright and transparency requirements.
key_points: GPAI providers must maintain technical documentation
Downstream deployers need sufficient information for compliant use
Copyright compliance and training-data summaries are recurring obligations
Systemic-risk GPAI models face added evaluation and incident-reporting duties
Cybersecurity and risk mitigation become explicit governance requirements
articles.use_case: Policy design for model providers and API integrators

articles.title: High-risk AI requires operational controls, not just legal review
articles.summary: For high-risk systems, compliance is inseparable from engineering, data governance, monitoring, and documentation practices.
key_points: High-risk systems require formal risk management and data governance
Technical documentation and logging must support audits and traceability
Human oversight needs to be designed into workflows
Conformity assessment, registration, and CE marking may apply
Post-market monitoring is part of the lifecycle, not an afterthought
articles.use_case: Compliance-by-design for product and engineering teams

articles.title: Penalties make AI governance a board-level issue
articles.summary: Potential penalties under the EU AI Act are large enough that AI compliance is now a governance, procurement, and enterprise risk management topic.
key_points: Penalty ranges are repeatedly cited up to €35M or 7% of global turnover for severe violations
Lesser breaches still carry material penalties, including multi-million-euro exposure
Vendor management and contracting must reflect AI risk categories
Model inventories and use-case classification are essential baseline controls
Cross-functional governance committees help align legal, security, data, and product teams
